ms.promise:
This milestone will output the Staking Basket technical specification. This smart-contract will allow users to deposit ADA into the smart-contract that delegates to multiple stakepools at the same time.

This specification will detail how anyone can use this code to create a Basket with their own list of stakepool hashes. They can determine the total number of pools the Basket delegates to, take a fee from the Basket, and add/remove pools epoch to epoch. This smart-contract allows addresses to deposit ADA and mints Basket tokens to the depositing address. These Basket tokens can be used to withdraw ADA + Staking rewards from the Basket. This smart-contract can delegate the ADA deposits to over 100 stakepools at the same time.

While this is purely a technical specification, a reviewer is asking us to clarify what network this smart-contract will be on to be approved. This smart-contract will be live on Cardano's preview network.
ms.criteria:
This milestone should be accepted given that we provide a technical specification for the Staking Basket smart-contract.

For this milestone to be accepted, the technical specification should detail the exact functionality of the smart-contract mentioned in the output.
ms.report:
Here is a link to the PDF file that is a technical specification for the Staking Basket smart-contract:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KxwoRnckRXEGE9p_twNO8-rnTp2W5C_sDpXb4CXPQAc/edit?usp=sharing
This technical specification is not a guide on how to create a Staking Basket, as that will not be possible until milestone 4. This technical specification shows that users can use this contract to create a Staking Basket that delegates to multiple pools using the code that's build from this technical specification. However, it does not show how to create a Basket. In the github in milestone four, there will be a page that someone can create locally that allows Basket creation.

A reviewer mentioned a guide for using the code is needed for this first milestone output. We will expand upon this to ensure a better UX when working with the contract. However if you have technical knowledge and the contract code this guide is sufficient. 
# Atrium

## Onchain

### Editing `onchain`

It is important, that any changes that change generated scripts are going to be incompatible with currently running baskets. 
Note, that changing onchain code haskell comments, or rearranging haskell code may also affect generated scripts, as Plutarch refer to source line numbers in it's error traces.

## Offchain

### How to run contracts using Eternl wallet:

You must have webpack dev server started:
```
atrium/offchain$ make dev-browser
```
When runned, dev browser will print out URL of a webpage from which you can interact with Atrium smart contracts using `preview` testnet

Eternl wallet setup:
- you must have Eternl wallet connected
- collateral must be set
- single-address option must be turned on

### How to add a dependency package (from `pursuit`):
```
atrium/offchain$ spago install <package-name>
atrium/offchain$ make spago2nix
atrium/offchain$ make build
```
For example, let's add a package `purescript-console`:
```
atrium/offchain$ spago install console
atrium/offchain$ make spago2ni

ms.promise:
In this milestone we’ll submit the Staking Basket audit report. This audit will ensure that the Staking Basket code was completed correctly, and that the smart-contract is secure.

We're working with an auditing firm Anastasia Labs. They've done multiple audits in this ecosystem and will ensure this smart-contract is secure. This audit will verify that it's impossible for the contract to be hacked, it'll verify that all of the features mentioned in the technical specification are possible.
ms.criteria:
This milestone should be accepted given that we provide a real audit report from a third party that specializes on Cardano’s smart-contract language audits.

This audit report needs to detail any issues found during the audit. The audit will also detail any small improvements that could be added to reduce fees, and ensure the contract works as Cardano's parameters change from DAO votes.
ms.report:
Atrium Labs engaged Anastasia Labs to evaluate and conduct a security assessment of its Atrium protocol. All code revision was performed following industry best practices.
Phases of code auditing activities include the following:
• Planning – Customer goals are gathered.
• Discovery – Perform code review to identify potential vulnerabilities, weak areas, and
exploits.
• Attack – Confirm potential vulnerabilities through testing and perform additional dis-
covery upon new access.
• Reporting – Document all found vulnerabilities.

The engineering team has also conducted a comprehensive review of protocol optimiza-
tion strategies.

Findings - You can read detailed overviews of findings by clicking the link to the audit report below.
ID-301 Insufficient field level datum comparisons . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 9
ID-302 Hard-coded Minimum Ada Constant . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 10
ID-101 Optimization: Unnecessary Plutarch Level Functions . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 11
ID-102 Optimization: Avoid Maybe types in on-chain code . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 12
ID-103 Optimization: Prefer consolidated fast-fail logic over perrorIfFalse . . . . . 13

You can view the entire detailed audit report by clicking this link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/13UQwVOIng3PlunWS6Ul9l9bZqWbiyKyN/view?usp=sharing
